identity.title: Sharp Bound for the Erdős–Straus Non-averaging Set Problem

assessment: Major revision required: three proved core proof/structural defects and four local findings in the exact assigned version. No counterexample to the main non-averaging bound is established.
outcome: Three confirmed Major and four confirmed Minor findings. Exact-source initial scientific review complete; independent scientific acceptance pending.

problems.title: The retained coefficient mass and doubled zonotope centre fail
problems.location: pp.13-15, (13), Lemma14 proof and Theorem4 after (15)
problems.hypotheses_checked: A=[-M,M], N=2M+1, P(A)=A, Ahat=A, A0=B=[0,2M], a=M. Explicit four-block E of at most s=N/log^2N elements verifies the structural conclusion. Uniform reduced-rank counting for every T of size>=delta N and every shift proves (delta,gamma)-irreducibility for fixed gamma<=delta/2. Choose fixed delta,gamma below the required powers and N sufficiently large. L=floor(M/10), mu=2L/N; coefficients 1/(2L) at M+-i, 1<=i<=L, and zero otherwise satisfy mass1, barycentre0 and exact cap.
problems.decisive_evidence: Permitted alternating order gives A1-a={-M,...,-L-1} union {1,...,L}. A 90% retained subset has coefficient mass0, so its centred zonotope is{0} and the proof's lower bound mu N/4 is false. The p.15 doubled centre is L(L+1)/2=max Z_(A1-a); the alleged positive B-neighbourhood leaves even the full zonotope. Allowed O(N/log N) deletions change the centre by O(N^2/log N), smaller than the positive c' mu gamma N B displacement for large N. Finite exact M1000 computation gives mass0 versus50 and doubled centre5050 at the endpoint.
problems.impact: A core step establishing Theorem4 and hence the main iteration is false as written.
problems.repair: Use actual small deletions and their retained coefficient mass>=1/3, a consistent interior scaling such as mu|A0|/4, and prove the inclusion in the retained zonotope. Track symmetric displacement bodies, rank-deficient slices, counting endpoint terms and at least two lattice points.
problems.repair_limit: The weaker printed Lemma14 statement with the full zonotope is not disproved by the zero-mass subset alone. Theorem4's conclusion and the main theorems are not refuted. Remaining geometric/lattice repair is not certified complete.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Theorem4 and coefficient ordering p.13, Lemma14 and its mass proof p.14, actual trimming/(15)/centre application p.15. Images distinguish barred retained zonotopes from the full zonotope and the factor1/2.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: For A=[-M,M], N=2M+1, choose P(A)=A, Ahat=A and identification x->x+M. The four-block E using k=floor(s/4) low and high signed integers has at most s points and subset sums covering[-k(M+1),k(M+1)], hence c0sP(A) for fixed c0<=1/100 and large M. For every T of size t>=delta N and every shift x in[0,2M], the reduced structural progression has at least t/2 points; rank r>=2 would force s(T)^r t=O(Ns(T)), impossible uniformly. Thus coherent rank-one choices give irreducibility with gamma<=delta/2. Fixed delta,gamma below the required powers satisfy the logarithmic lower bound for sufficiently large N.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Set L=floor(M/10), mu=2L/N, and coefficients1/(2L) at M+-i for1<=i<=L, zero elsewhere. They satisfy the cap, mass1 and zero barycentre; the median is not mu-convex. The allowed alternating order gives A1-a={-M,...,-L-1} union{1,...,L}. Retaining only the first part keeps at least90% of A1 but zero coefficient mass, so the stronger centred retained zonotope is{0} and cannot contain xi NB. Independently, the p.15 doubled centre sum is L(L+1)/2, the maximum of the full zonotope. Permitted O(N/log N) deletions change it by only O(N^2/log N), whereas the positive fixed-xi displacement has order xi N^2, so the p.15 inclusion still fails after the actual trimming. Exact M1000 arithmetic gives[-495450,5050], centre5050, half-centre2525, and mass0 versus50.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The zero-mass subset alone does not refute the weaker literal Lemma14 statement with the full zonotope. The interval has averaging relations and does not refute Theorem4's conclusion.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: False retained-mass inference and false centre inclusion occur in the core irreducibility-to-intersecting-subset-sums argument, then Case3 of the main proof. Major without a main-theorem counterexample.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Alternating bounded coefficients gives about half mass on each full side; the actual small deletion loses O(1/(mu log N)), leaving at least1/3 for large N. A consistent interior scale mu|A0|/4 is a plausible start, but the retained inclusion, symmetric displacement body, slice-rank/lattice counting and two-point intersection still need proof. They are not certified repaired.

problems.title: Whole-step retention is substituted for preprocessing retention in the final product
problems.location: pp.17-18, Case3 and final cardinality verification
problems.hypotheses_checked: The actual preceding scalar bounds are Mnew>=c eta^p r M and Vnew<=C eta r^K V. Set d2, epsilon1/100, p103/300, K100, r1, eta=t^300 and whole-step rho=t^103.
problems.decisive_evidence: Both displayed one-step inequalities hold with constants1, but (Vnew/V)/rho^K=t^-10000 diverges. At t1/2 the exact ratio is2^10000. The inserted max(1,C rho^K) also equals1 for small rho and gives no lower bound on the product of rhos.
problems.impact: The printed proof does not preserve the large-set hypotheses through its iteration, a core termination/parameter requirement.
problems.repair: Keep eta and r separate. The report proves a conditional positive-power size bound using F=log M-(alpha_d+2epsilon)log V and a nonnegative increment epsilon log(1/eta)+(Kpstar-1)log(1/r)-O(1).
problems.repair_limit: This is a disproof of an inference from scalar estimates, not an actual non-averaging-set counterexample. The potential repair is conditional on the corrected geometric Case3, and does not assert the exact printed near-original exponent.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Case3 pp.17-18 has a preprocessing ratio and an additional geometric eta; the final paragraph redefines rho_j as the entire step's cardinality ratio.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: The available bounds are Mnew>=c eta^p rM and Vnew<=C eta r^K V, p=(d-1)/(d+1)+epsilon. For d2, epsilon1/100,K100,r1 take eta=t^300,rho=t^103, Vnew/V=eta and Mnew/M=rho. Sizes can be scaled to meet integer and polynomial lower bounds.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The one-step bounds hold with constants1, but (Vnew/V)/rho^K=t^-10000 diverges. The product with max(1,C rho_j^K) gives no lower bound on product rho_j when those maxima equal1. A lower bound on retained size does not establish the claimed upper bound rho_j<=mu^c.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This is a counterexample to an algebraic inference, not a realized non-averaging configuration. A different bookkeeping argument can preserve sufficient size.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Persistence of the size and common parameters is required throughout the contradiction iteration; the printed proof does not establish it. Major core derivation error.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Conditional on correct geometric Case3, set pstar=alpha_d+2epsilon<1 and F=log M-pstar log V. Its increment is at least epsilon log(1/eta)+(Kpstar-1)log(1/r)-O(1)>=0 for large input. Entry surplus bounds F below by a positive multiple of log Mentry; M<=V bounds it above by(1-pstar)log M. Bounded dimension changes yield a positive-power size bound and common log-log scales. This proves neither the precise near-original exponent nor the unresolved geometric step.

problems.title: Lemma6 lacks an origin condition and is false for affine containing GAPs
problems.location: p.10 Lemma6; pp.11-13 uses; AppendixA initial translation p.19
problems.hypotheses_checked: A=N+[1,m], N=m^4, input Paff=A has rank1 and size m. With s=m/log^2m and t=floor(s/2), Ahat=A, P0={uN+v:|u|<=1,|v|<=m} is proper rank2 and contains A and0. The low/high t-element blocks give a homogeneous translate of c0 sP0 in their subset sums for every fixed c0<=1/100 and large m. All structural conclusions and polynomial box-size conditions are proved.
problems.decisive_evidence: Fixed-cardinality block sums fill explicit overlapping integer intervals, giving x0+c0sP0 within Sigma(A'). Yet |P0|=3(2m+1), while Lemma6 claims O(m/s). The ratio grows like s. A separate rank-one impossibility proof shows the origin cannot be handled by choosing a rank-one structural progression. The finite certificate checks113157 interval endpoint inequalities; the asymptotic proof defeats the unspecified constant.
problems.impact: False structural lemma supplies the up-move savings used in the main reduction.
problems.repair: Require an origin-containing centered input GAP, delete width-one coordinates, and recheck every use with the origin fixed. A translation of A cannot silently transport variable-cardinality subset sums.
problems.repair_limit: No non-averaging assumption appears in Lemma6, so the interval witness meets its actual scope. The main theorem is not refuted; a complete repair of all origin-sensitive applications is not asserted.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: GAPs are explicitly affine on p.9, while Lemma6 p.10 assumes only A subset P. The proof incorrectly puts all shorter subset sums in sP. Structural outputs contain0; the arbitrary input P need not.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: A=N+[1,m],N=m^4 and Paff=A have a box of size m (also after embedding in Z2). The allowed output P0={uN+v:|u|<=1,|v|<=m} contains A and0, has rank2 and size3(2m+1), and its c0s dilate is proper for fixed c0<=1/100. Take low/high blocks with t=floor(s/2),2t<=s.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: At fixed total cardinality k, low/high block sums fill the explicit intervals[L_(k,h),U_(k,h)]. For |k-t|<=c0s and t/3<=h<=2t/3 their lengths exceed13t^2/36, adjacent endpoints differ by m+O(t), and t^2/m tends to infinity. Their union covers[.4tm,.6tm]; hence x0=tN+floor(tm/2) plus c0sP0 lies in the subset sums. All structural requirements therefore hold, yet Lemma6 would require3(2m+1)=O(m/s). A rank-one origin-containing GAP covering more than(m+1)/2 points must have step1 and span at least N; its long dilate cannot fit the separated fixed-cardinality bands of subset sums. Thus choosing rank one does not remove the problem. New exact checks cover113157 finite intervals, while the arbitrary-large proof supplies the unspecified-threshold argument.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Lemma6 has no non-averaging premise. This interval example therefore fits its scope but supplies no counterexample to the main theorem. Width-one coordinates are removed in growth estimates.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: A false structural lemma is used for up-move savings and iteration bounds in Lemma10, hence Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Require an origin-containing centered input progression and keep that origin fixed through uses. The initial Appendix A translation of an arbitrary box also needs justification for variable-cardinality subset sums; a complete repair of all applications is not asserted.

problems.title: Affine approximation and nonempty-index wording in Lemma2
problems.hypotheses_checked: d2,m1000,c1,I=[m],H identically1 on(-1,2) is bounded convex and c>2d/m.
problems.decisive_evidence: Best strict-linear error on Qv is1/(2v+1)>=1/2001, larger than64/10^6=1/15625. Affine approximation has error0. Empty I also cannot supply v. The report gives a full overlap-multiplicity proof for the intended affine estimate with constant3d^3(d-1)<4d^4.
problems.impact: Literal strict-linear statement and proof wording are false or incomplete; intended local estimate survives.
problems.repair: Say affine, require nonempty I, evaluate at v/m, and use coordinatewise derivative variation with overlap at most d. Smooth with arbitrarily small domain loss.
problems.repair_limit: No failure of the corrected density exponent is claimed.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Lemma2 p.4 uses linear and allows arbitrary I; Claim3 p.5 says no function at all and evaluates the gradient at v, while its calculation needs v/m. The p.6 telescoping misses an endpoint.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: d2,m1000,c1,I=[m],H=1 on(-1,2) satisfy all displayed domain, range and convexity assumptions.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: For strictly linear ax on Qv, balancing endpoint errors gives minimum1/(2v+1)>=1/2001, exceeding the printed1/15625. Affine H itself has zero error. I empty cannot supply v. For the corrected affine proof, each bad cube supplies a coordinate derivative increment>=Delta m/d^2. Each coordinate line's segments overlap at most d, and derivative variation on the relevant interval is at most3/c, yielding Delta<=3d^3(d-1)m^(d-3)/(c|I|)<4d^4m^(d-3)/(c|I|).
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: If linear is intended colloquially to include affine, this is a terminology correction. Convex smoothing with arbitrarily small domain loss and the strict constant slack completes the corrected argument; d1 is immediate.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Local statement/proof normalization with complete bounded repair, Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Say affine, require nonempty I, use gradient at v/m and the overlap variation proof.

problems.title: Width, inverse coordinates and density normalization in Lemma1
problems.location: p.7 width and H rescaling; p.9 small-K final display
problems.hypotheses_checked: For the intermediate convex-geometric implication, an equilateral triangle has width h and inradius h/3. The rescaling is exactly H(x)=1-h(u(2x-1))/(2sqrt(d)). Every selected mass fraction |A intersect Omega''|/|A| is at most1.
problems.decisive_evidence: Width does not give inradius w/2. Inverting the displayed map gives y/(2u)+1/2, not +1; u1/4,y0 maps to y1/4 under the printed inverse. The p.9 first-case final line drops eta^(-alpha-epsilon) and asserts an impossible fraction>1.
problems.impact: Intermediate normalizations are false, but bounded constant/coordinate corrections retain the intended density increment.
problems.repair: Use a dimension-dependent inradius constant, the half-unit translation and the normalized density fraction. Account for bounded overlap and use an enclosing vertical interval/upper volume bound in the flat case.
problems.repair_limit: The geometric examples refute the specified intermediate assertions, not the full corrected Lemma1. Other rank/geometry concerns without a witness under full irreducibility are kept as clarifications.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Width-to-ball and inverse-coordinate step p.7; first-case normalized-density chain pp.8-9 and its final unnormalized line.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: An equilateral triangle has minimum width h and inradius h/3, contradicting the general w/2 implication. The actual change is H(x)=1-h(u(2x-1))/(2sqrt d). Any selected mass fraction is<=1.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Inverse coordinates are y/(2u)+1/2, not +1; u1/4,y0 demonstrates the mismatch. The final p.9 first-case mass fraction is erroneously bounded below by a quantity tending to infinity; its preceding eta^(-alpha-epsilon) factor must remain. A dimensional inradius constant suffices by the inscribed-ellipsoid comparison. Bounded box overlap handles coincident boundary representatives; an enclosing vertical interval avoids zero-height volume comparison.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: These examples refute intermediate assertions, not corrected Lemma1. The first-case gain is delta^(-.1epsilon) up to constants. In the large-K repair the actual m^(d epsilon) factor, together with u^((d-1)(2/(d+1)-epsilon)), gives delta exponent -epsilon(d+2)/(10(d+1))-(d-1)epsilon^2/10<0, so no extra m^epsilon is needed. This algebra was independently checked.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Constant, coordinate and normalization corrections retain exponent slack; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use a dimension-dependent inscribed radius, half-unit translation, normalized fraction, bounded multiplicities and upper volume bound; intersect the final body with the original body. No unrestricted thin-strip example is promoted to a full-irreducibility counterexample.

problems.title: Adjoining zero destroys non-averaging of the retained image
problems.location: p.10 first sentence of Section3.1; p.11 identification-domain wording
problems.hypotheses_checked: For arbitrary large m, N=m^3 and pi=(N+i,(N+i)^2), take A={pi,2pi:1<=i<=m}. It has2m points and an O(m^9) box, hence fixed (2,10) parameters. First-coordinate separation forces any average's coefficients all equal, then variance forces all indices equal, proving A non-averaging.
problems.decisive_evidence: Every retained subset of more than m points contains a doubling pair. Corollary5 retains more than m points for large m, so adding0 creates pi=(0+2pi)/2. Proper csP with cs>=2 makes the identification preserve this relation. Exact m8 enumeration checked65535 subsets with no average in A and all8 doubling pairs.
problems.impact: The introductory reduction claim is false even under the structural deletion and polynomial box conditions; actual later use omits0.
problems.repair: Claim non-averaging only for phiP(Ahat), retaining0 solely in the bounding progression; restrict identification domains to the retained set until containment is arranged.
problems.repair_limit: The later reduction already uses the unaugmented image, so this is local and does not refute the main theorem.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: The first sentence of Section3.1 p.10 asserts non-averaging after adjoining0. Actual Lemma10 p.11 uses the unaugmented retained image.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: For m>4,N=m^3,pi=(N+i,(N+i)^2),A={pi,2pi:1<=i<=m} has2m distinct points in an O(m^9) box, hence fixed(2,10) parameters for large m. Corollary5 retains more than m points.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: In an average equal to c pi0, the first coordinate forces sum c_j=kc because the error is<4m^2<N. Since c,c_j in{1,2}, all c_j=c. Remaining first and second coordinates force sum(i_j-i0)^2=0, impossible with the target excluded. Thus A is non-averaging. Every retained subset larger than m contains a pair pi,2pi, so adjoining0 creates pi=(0+2pi)/2. Centered csP proper with cs>=2 makes identification preserve this relation.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The inverse identification is affine, so the unaugmented image remains non-averaging. The manuscript's later reduction already uses it. The old finite exhaustive test is retained but not claimed newly executed.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: False introductory/domain assertion with a local repair, Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Keep0 in the progression for subset-sum structure, and claim non-averaging only for phiP(Ahat). Restrict Definition9's identification domain to retained points unless containment has first been arranged.
